evidence.description: Actions as permutation homomorphisms; orbits and kernels

sections.title: What this reference adds
sections.text: A concise algebra reference for readers already comfortable with undergraduate groups. The selected pages connect set actions to linear representations and explain why finite-group representations often break into simpler invariant pieces.

sections.title: Two distinctions worth retaining
sections.text: An action is faithful when no nonidentity element fixes everything. It is free when every point stabilizer is trivial. These are different requirements. A representation is an action by invertible linear maps.

sections.title: How the proof works
sections.text: Maschke’s theorem constructs an invariant complement to an invariant subspace by averaging a projector over the group. Over real or complex spaces, averaging an appropriate positive-definite form provides another approach.

sections.title: Conclusion and hypothesis
sections.text: For finite G, if the field characteristic does not divide |G|, every invariant subspace has an invariant complement. The division by |G| in the averaging formula explains why that field condition matters.

sections.title: Why this is a useful bridge
sections.text: An action gives a homomorphism into permutations; requiring linear maps gives a homomorphism into GL(V). This is the transition from visual symmetry to the representation language used in moonshine.
